crit: No reason is given for the three UCI data sets (Pima, Satimage, Haberman). The simulated Circle data set is introduced so that 'our methods can be easily understood' (illustration of which borderline minority examples are over-sampled) and is then reused in the experiments.
notes: Only 4 data sets. The sole stated rationale concerns the illustrative simulated Circle set (coded own reason/analytic); if the adjudicator does not count an illustration purpose as a selection rationale, crit_type would be 'not stated'. 'All the attributes in the data sets are quantitative' is a description, not stated as a selection reason. Table 2 prints 'Percentage of minority class' rather than an IR, and has no n_classes or n_minority column. modified_data_released = no: no link, repository, supplement or availability statement in the paper (only the UCI repository URL in reference [24]); the only author modification is the Satimage class-4-vs-rest binarisation. Results are shown only as line plots (Fig. 2), no numeric results tables.
